questions.stem:
Figure 1 shows a sketch of the graph with equation $y = \mathrm{f}(x)$ where
$\mathrm{f}(x) = 2|x-5|+10$
The point $P$, shown in Figure 1, is the vertex of the graph.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) State the coordinates of $P$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: One correct coordinate. Allow as $x=5$ or $y=10$. Do not allow them to be the wrong way round.
B1: Both coordinates correct $(5,10)$. Allow as $x=5, y=10$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Condone missing brackets around pairs of coordinates provided the meaning is clear
- If there is a contradiction between coordinates on the graph, by the question and in the main body of the work then the work in the main body of the work takes precedence.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use algebra to solve
$2|x-5|+10 > 6x$
(Solutions relying on calculator technology are not acceptable.)
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) Answers with no working score 0 marks.
M1: Attempts to solve a correct equation or inequality with at least one intermediate stage of working. Allow this mark even if there are additional equations/inequalities. The modulus signs must have been removed. Alternatively, may attempt to square both sides and then attempt to solve the quadratic (usual rules apply). If via a calculator the root(s) must be correct.
A1: $x < \frac{5}{2}$ o.e. only. isw if they attempt to simplify their fraction incorrectly. Must be identified as their only inequality e.g. circling, underlining. Allow other forms such as $x \in (-\infty, \frac{5}{2})$. Do not accept $x \leqslant \frac{5}{2}$. Do not withhold this mark for incorrect use of inequality signs in earlier work provided the final answer is correct.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Attempts to solve e.g. $-2(x-5)+10...6x \Rightarrow x..."\frac{5}{2}"$ M1
- If via a calculator the root(s) must be correct (you may need to check these) Condone slips including when squaring and multiplying out $|x-5|...3x-5 \Rightarrow x^2-10x+25...9x^2-30x+25 \Rightarrow 0...8x^2-20x \Rightarrow x...$
- In either method condone slips in their rearrangement and do not be concerned by the direction of the inequality sign for this mark.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the point to which $P$ is mapped, when the graph with equation $y = \mathrm{f}(x)$ is transformed to the graph with equation $y = 3\mathrm{f}(x-2)$
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) B1ft: One correct coordinate. Allow as $x=7$ or $y=30$. Follow through on their $((a)+2,(a)\times 3)$ Allow as $x=(a)+2$ or $y=(a)\times 3$ (does not have to be evaluated).
B1ft: Correct coordinates $(7,30)$. Allow as $x=7, y=30$ or correct ft $((a)+2,(a)\times 3)$. Allow as $x=(a)+2, y=(a)\times 3$ (must be evaluated)

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write $\mathrm{g}(x)$ in the form
$Ax + B + \dfrac{C}{x-2}$
where $A$, $B$ and $C$ are integers to be found.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Sets $2x^2-5x+8 = (Ax+B)(x-2)+C$ with an attempt at one constant.
dM1: Attempts all 3 constants. E.g. sets $x=2 \Rightarrow C=..., -2B+C=8 \Rightarrow B=...$ and compares $x^2$ terms gives $A=...$
A1: $2x-1+\dfrac{6}{x-2}$
Official notes (completeness pass):
- ANSWERS IN (a) of $A=2, B=-5, C=2$, and/or $28+2\ln3$ in (b) please send to review
- Note that correct values for A, B, and C imply the first two marks
- M1: Note that if an identity is used it must be correct. Condone arithmetical slips when evaluating. The identity may be implied by correct equations e.g. $x^2: A=2,\ x: -2A+B=-5,\ \text{constant}: -2B+C=8$
- M1: division is used look for a quotient as far as $2x$. Note that the division may appear in many different formats or may be by inspection so $2x$ is sufficient to score this mark. e.g. $\frac{2x^2-5x+8}{x-2}=\frac{2x(x-2)+4x-5x+8}{x-2}=2x+\frac{-(x-2)-2+8}{x-2}=2x-1+\frac{6}{x-2}$
- dM1: Attempts to find all 3 constants which are all non-zero. It is dependent upon the previous mark. Via an identity: If three simultaneous equations are formed allow this mark to be scored for proceeding to values for A, B and C. You do not need to check this. Allow sign slips only in forming the equations. Via division: Look for a quotient of $2x\pm c$ and a constant remainder
- A1: The expression must be written; it cannot be awarded for just stating the correct values of A, B and C, unless it is later written correctly as an expression in (b) (may be seen within an integral)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Hence use algebraic integration to show that
$\displaystyle\int_{4}^{8} \mathrm{g}(x)\,dx = \alpha + \beta\ln 3$
where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are integers to be found.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: Attempts to integrate the term $\dfrac{C}{x-2}$ proceeding to $D\ln|x-2|$.
A1ft: Correct integration of $\mathrm{g}(x)$ for their $A$, $B$ and $C$ from part (a): $\dfrac{Ax^2}{2}+Bx+C\ln|x-2|$ o.e.
dM1: Attempts to proceed to the form $p+q\ln r$ by using the limits 8 and 4 in an expression of the form $Ex^2+Fx+D\ln|x-2|$ o.e. and subtracting either way round, and combining their ln terms correctly.
A1: $44+6\ln3$. Withhold the final mark if there is an integral and dx around the answer or $+c$.
Alt via substitution $u=x-2$: M1: correct attempt to integrate $\dfrac{C}{u}$ to $D\ln|u|$; A1ft: $A(u+2)+B+\dfrac{C}{u}$; dM1: substitutes limits 6 and 2, subtracts, combines ln terms; A1: $44+6\ln3$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: C does not have to be equal D (do not be concerned with brackets or modulus sign)
- A1ft: (where $A,B,C\neq0$) which may be unsimplified with or without a constant of integration. Do not be concerned by the absence of the bracket or modulus on the $x-2$ (as both values substituted in will give positive lns)
- dM1: (where $D,E,F\neq0$) combining their ln terms correctly. e.g. this mark cannot be scored for $\ln6-\ln2=\frac{\ln6}{\ln2}=\ln3$ but treat as a sign slip in front of the log rather than incorrect log work e.g. $6\ln6-6\ln2=-6\ln3$. Condone slips when evaluating or multiplying out brackets only (condone a spurious + c present for this mark). The substitution and combining of their ln terms can be implied by their $p+q\ln r$ provided no incorrect log work is seen. Note that ln r does not have to be ln 3 e.g. it may be ln 729.
- Alt A1ft: $A(u+2)+B+\frac{C}{u}\Rightarrow\frac{Au^2}{2}+(2A+B)x+C\ln|u|$ or condone $\frac{Ax^2}{2}+Bx+C\ln|u|$. dM1: or substitutes back to an expression in terms of x and proceeds as in the main scheme and notes. If they are working in a mixture of variables, $x^2-x+6\ln u$ then the correct limits must be substituted into the appropriate terms.

parts.label: i
parts.text:
(i) The variables $x$ and $y$ are connected by the equation
$y = \dfrac{10^6}{x^3} \qquad x>0$
Sketch the graph of $\log_{10}y$ against $\log_{10}x$
Show on your sketch the coordinates of the points of intersection of the graph with the axes.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(i) $y=\dfrac{10^6}{x^3} \Rightarrow \log_{10}y = \log_{10}10^6 - \log_{10}x^3 \Rightarrow \log_{10}y = 6-3\log_{10}x$
B1: For a straight line with negative gradient anywhere on a set of axes. It must intersect both axes and not stop at these points. Do not penalise if the line is not perfectly straight and do not be concerned with the steepness provided there is no intention to draw a curve or a horizontal line. Axes do not need to be labelled but if they are then the y-axis needs to be $\log y$ and the horizontal axis must be $\log x$ (with or without base 10 labelled).
B1: For an intercept of 6 on the $\log_{10}y$ axis for their graph. Can be labelled as just 6 instead of $(0,6)$. The line must pass through (or start/stop at) this point.
B1: For an intercept of 2 on the $\log_{10}x$ axis for their graph. Can be labelled as just 2 instead of $(2,0)$. The line must pass through (or start/stop at) this point.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Condone invisible brackets around coordinates provided the meaning is clear. Coordinates may be stated away from the graph which is fine provided a graph is drawn. Note that they may draw a curve so B0B1B1 is possible as the marks are earned independently of each other. Note that if they draw on Figure 2 the axis labels are incorrect so maximum score is B0B1B1
- B1: Condone y intercept labelled as $(6, 0)$ provided the point is on the positive y-axis. Do not be concerned by the axis labelling for this mark.
- B1: Condone x intercept being labelled as $(0, 2)$ provided the point is on the positive x-axis. Do not be concerned by the axis labelling for this mark.

parts.label: ii
parts.text:
(ii) Figure 2 shows the linear relationship between $\log_3 N$ and $t$.
Show that $N = ab^t$ where $a$ and $b$ are constants to be found.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(ii) Note that $N=81\times9^t$ with no working is 0 marks. May work in terms of $x$ instead of $t$ which is fine, but the final answer must be in terms of $t$.
B1: States $\log_3N=2t+4$ (which may be left unsimplified) or states $\log_3N=\log_3a+t\log_3b$. Condone lack of base 3 written but base 10 is B0.
M1: For using the laws of logs correctly and moving from $\log_3N=at+b$ to $N=3^{at}\times3^b$. If they write $3^{2t}+3^4$ then M0A0 but if it is ambiguous between $+$ and $\times$ give the benefit of the doubt.
A1cso: $N=81\times9^t$. Just stating the values of $a$ and $b$ does not score this mark. We must see $\log_3N=2t+4$ or $N=3^{2t+4}$ or $N=3^{2t}\times3^4$ before proceeding to the answer with no incorrect log work seen, or both $\log_3a=4\Rightarrow a=3^4$ o.e. and $\log_3b=2\Rightarrow b=3^2$ o.e. before proceeding to $N=81\times9^t$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- $N=3^{2t+4}=3^{2t}\times3^4$ or $\log_3a=4\Rightarrow a=...$ or $\log_3b=2\Rightarrow b=...$ M1
- A misread writing a different base to 3 (including 10) can score a maximum B0M1A0.
- B1: May be implied by further work which is not the final answer. If they write down an incorrect equation e.g. $\log_3N=-2t+4$ as well as $\log_3N=\log_3a+t\log_3b$ then allow this mark to be scored.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Write $\mathrm{f}(x)$ in the form
$a\sin2x + b\cos2x + c$
where $a$, $b$ and $c$ are integers to be found.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: States or uses $\sin2x=2\sin x\cos x$ or $\cos2x=\pm2\cos^2x\pm1$.
dM1: Uses $\sin2x=2\sin x\cos x$ and $\cos2x=\pm2\cos^2x\pm1$ in $\mathrm{f}(x)$ to produce an expression of the required form $a\sin2x+b\cos2x+c$.
A1: $4\sin2x+2\cos2x-1$. Correct answer scores all three marks. Must be in terms of $x$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- For the method marks condone working in mixed variables provided the intention is clear
- M1: (may be implied by use of e.g. $\cos^2x=\pm1\pm\sin^2x$ and $\cos2x=\pm1\pm2\sin^2x$ or $\cos2x=\pm\cos^2x\pm\sin^2x$) Can be implied by either of $a=4$; $b=\pm2$ and $c=-5$ or $-1$
- dM1: Condone slips when substituting in. Can be implied by $a=4$ and $b=\pm2$ and $c=-5$ or $-1$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Use the answer to part (a) to write $\mathrm{f}(x)$ in the form
$R\sin(2x+\alpha) + c$
where $R>0$ and $0<\alpha<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
Give the exact value of $R$ and give the value of $\alpha$ in radians to 3 significant figures.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) Full marks can only be scored provided correct values for $a,b,c$ are found in (a).
B1ft: Finds the exact value of $R$ using $R^2=a^2+b^2\Rightarrow R=\sqrt{20}$ or $2\sqrt5$.
M1: Uses a correct method to find $\alpha$ using their $a$ and $b$, e.g. $\tan\alpha=\pm\dfrac{b}{a}\Rightarrow \alpha=...$
A1cso: $2\sqrt5\sin(2x+\text{awrt }0.464)-1$ o.e. e.g. $\sqrt{20}\sin(2x+0.464)-1$. Can only be scored provided correct values for $a,b,c$ are found in (a).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1ft: (or may use trigonometry using their value for $\alpha$) Can be implied by a correct exact value. Follow through on their a or b but the correct values should give $R=\sqrt{20}$ or $2\sqrt5$
- M1: or $\tan\alpha=\pm\frac{a}{b}\Rightarrow\alpha=...$ (You may need to check this on your calculator if only the angle is seen) May also be seen using e.g. $\sin\alpha=\pm\frac{b}{"R"}\Rightarrow\alpha=...$ or $\cos\alpha=\pm\frac{a}{"R"}\Rightarrow\alpha=...$ Allow the angle to be found in degrees for this mark. $\alpha=$"awrt 26.6°" (1dp)
